brief: Two catalysts drove the week's sharpest moves: CoreWeave co-founder McBee's reported comments (FT) on insurance's near-unlimited capital availability, and a sharper debate on frontier labs' business-model economics and closed-vs-open competition. Both fed AI-related neocloud/frontier-lab corporate bond funding-cost concerns, which GS credit research calls the epicentre of the debate. Bonds rallied and yields broke lower Thursday (GS had upgraded bonds to Overweight Monday). Equity momentum (price, positioning, sentiment) has been negative since end of Q2: AI stocks were sold for a sixth straight day, the AI-winners-vs-AI-at-risk trade and momentum factor have halved from their June peaks and are retesting lows, and CoreWeave is testing July lows. GS argues this reflects already-priced capex/earnings deceleration, not thesis reversal, since compute demand and pricing show no actual slowdown, and the momentum pendulum may have swung too far negative. It reiterates that Q3 earnings will show the biggest AI spenders' ROI and self-funding ability, a leadership flip from AI-spend beneficiaries to AI investors, citing Sarah Friar on compute scarcity. It also flags unexpectedly modest IG/HY issuance estimates and a 2027 equity-supply debate: large net supply from lockup expirations, but still under 1% of market cap, a level the 1990s exceeded without hurting index performance.
